samples.summary: Slides mobile toolbar's B/I/U toggles still decide from `getSelectionStyle()` — the exact #715 mechanism the diff fixes, left in place on a shared-editor surface
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/mobile-toolbar.tsx:225-234` still does `textEditor.applyStyle({ bold: !textEditor.getSelectionStyle().bold })` (and italic/underline), with `pressed={!!sel.bold}` from the same caret read at :240-253. `SlidesTextBoxEditor` exposes `getRangeStyleSummary()` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:240, delegating to packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1017), so the same backward-selection stuck-toggle bug is reachable there. Worse, the very same component renders `TextFormatSheet` → `TextFormatGroup` (mobile-toolbar.tsx:260, :552), which after this change decides from the range — so two Bold buttons in one bar now disagree. The task doc declares this out of scope (docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:60), but the fix is one-line and the sibling site is a consumer of the same interface.

samples.summary: Cmd/Ctrl+B/I/U/S keyboard path still inverts the caret style, so the keyboard now disagrees with the toolbar it used to match
samples.evidence: `TextEditor.toggleStyle` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2875-2895) resolves `const base = this.getStyleAtCursor()` and does `resolved[key] = !visual[key]` for the shortcuts wired at :872-902. With a backward selection the caret sits at the range start and resolves the preceding run — the identical #715 defect. After this change the toolbar button renders unpressed (range says not-bold) while Ctrl+B removes bold, i.e. two entry points to the same mutation now behave differently. Acknowledged as a known limitation in docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:52-56, but it is a reachable user path with no guard directing it through the new range-aware decision.

samples.summary: Every render of the shared TextFormatGroup now performs a full range walk (`getRangeStyleSummary()`), replacing an O(1) caret lookup, for all consumers including slides
samples.evidence: text-format-group.tsx:96 calls `editor?.getRangeStyleSummary()` unconditionally during render; the docs implementation (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2818-2900) walks every inline run in the selection and JSON.stringify-tokenizes each style key per run, and re-computes named-style defaults per block. Consumers re-render on every cursor move / store change (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:308-318; slides text-edit-section.tsx:83; mobile-toolbar.tsx:552), and each toggle handler calls the summary a second time. For a select-all over a large document this is per-render O(runs) work where the previous `getSelectionStyle()` was a single block lookup. No measurement done — flagging so the author can confirm it is acceptable.

samples.summary: Interface doc comments still describe `getSelectionStyle()` as the toolbar's style source, now stale for the B/I/U/S toggles
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/types.ts:21-22 documents `getSelectionStyle()` as "the inline style at the current cursor/selection anchor" with no note that boolean toggles must not use it; packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:606 still says the cursor-move notification exists so consumers can "use getSelectionStyle() to update bold/italic toggles", which is no longer how the shared toggles work. A reader implementing a new toolbar surface will reproduce #715 by following these comments.

verdict.reason: Verified directly. mobile-toolbar.tsx:223 reads `textEditor.getSelectionStyle()` and lines 225/228/231-233 invert that caret read to drive `applyStyle`, with `pressed` at :240/:245/:253 from the same read — the #715 caret mechanism, unchanged. The slides text-box editor does expose the range-aware alternative (`getRangeStyleSummary()` declared at packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:240-251), so the fix is available on this very object. The inconsistency claim also holds: the same TextEditMobileBar renders TextFormatSheet (mobile-toolbar.tsx:260) which passes the identical `textEditor` to `TextFormatGroup` (mobile-toolbar.tsx:552-556), and TextFormatGroup now derives both pressed state and applied value from `isStyleOn(editor.getRangeStyleSummary()...)` (text-format-group.tsx:96,100,106,113,120). Two Bold controls driven by one editor can therefore disagree on a backward or mixed selection. No refutation ground applies: not-present fails (code is verbatim), already-guarded fails (no caller-side guard; this is the mobile text-edit toolbar rendered for ToolbarState kind "text-edit"), and out-of-scope fails because this is a consumer of the same shared text-formatting interface left on the old contract — the blast-radius lane. The task doc's "out of scope" note (docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:60-61) is documentation data, not a technical refutation.

verdict.reason: Verified independently and the finding holds on every checkable point. (1) Code present as described: `TextEditor.toggleStyle` (text-editor.ts:2875-2895) resolves `const base = this.getStyleAtCursor()` (:2884) and inverts with `resolved[key] = !visual[key]` (:2891); `getStyleAtCursor` (:2967-2981) uses the `cursor.position.offset <= inlineEnd` match (:2974) — the same `<=` boundary the repo's todo (lines 15-18) names as the #715 mechanism that resolves the preceding run. (2) Shortcuts are wired to it at :872 (b), :878 (i), :884 (u), :890 (Cmd+Shift+X strikethrough), :896, :902. (3) Reachable, not dead code: TextEditor is constructed at editor.ts:2213 and text-box-editor.ts:666 and exported at index.ts:92; backward selections are a real state — handleMouseDown sets the caret to the drag/shift focus (text-editor.ts:1566) and selection.ts:174-180 normalises focus-before-anchor, so with a backward selection the caret sits at the range start. (4) The divergence is real: the toolbar entry point now decides via the range-aware summary (text-format-group.tsx:100,106,113,120 for the action; :163,181,199,218 for `pressed`, backed by editor.ts:2773-2814), while the keyboard path reaches the identical `doc.applyInlineStyle` mutation (text-editor.ts:2914) carrying the old caret-derived decision, with no guard routing it through the new logic. Two entry points to one mutation now behave differently — squarely the blast-radius lane (a changed decision contract with an un-updated second entry point), not diff-internal correctness. No refutation ground applies: the code is present, nothing guards the bypass, and it lies outside the diff so it is in scope for this lens. The todo's 'Out of scope' note (lines 52-56) is repository data documenting the author's intent; it corroborates the mechanism but cannot waive a reachable user-facing inconsistency or redefine reviewer scope. Minor wording slip in the finding's title (strikethrough is Cmd+Shift+X, not Cmd+S) does not affect the substance — the cited line numbers are correct.
